subject: Emotions
title: Psychological Safety
description: A fast breakdown of Psychological Safety for builders.

hook.text: Google spent millions on Project Aristotle to find what makes teams great. The answer wasn't talent or process.

buildup.text: Amy Edmondson discovered 'psychological safety'—the belief that you won't be punished for mistakes, questions, or ideas.

discovery.text: Safe teams don't make fewer errors. They report more errors—which means they catch problems before they escalate.

twist.text: Psychological safety isn't about being nice. It's about honesty without fear. Tough feedback happens in safe teams.

climax.text: One leader behavior builds safety above all: responding to vulnerability with curiosity, not criticism.

punchline.text: The best teams aren't fearless. They're safe enough to be afraid out loud.
